items.stem: Users must see the first words of a reply before the full answer is ready. The model and the answer quality must stay the same. Which change meets both constraints?
options: Stream the response, so text appears as the tokens arrive.
Enable fast mode, which cuts the time to first token.
Send each request as a Message Batch, and read the results the next day.
Cache each full answer in a custom store, and show it only after the answer is complete.
items.rationale: Streaming sends output as the model generates it, so the first words appear before the answer ends. Streaming does not reduce the total generation work (Inference).
items.trap: Fast mode looks like a first-token fix, but its speed gain applies to output tokens per second, not to time to first token.

items.stem: An evaluation run has 50,000 prompts. Results can arrive within one day, and the run must cost less than standard calls. No user waits for these results.
options: Send each prompt one at a time on the standard path, with high effort.
Buy a Priority Tier commitment, which gives half-price calls.
Submit one Message Batch, and also run the full set on the standard path.
Submit the prompts as one Message Batch, and read results after processing ends.
items.rationale: Batch usage is charged at half the standard API price. Results can take up to 24 hours, which fits an evaluation run that no user waits on.
items.trap: Standard calls look simple, but they keep standard pricing for a job that can wait a day.

items.stem: A classifier meets its accuracy floor at medium effort, but its latency target is tight. Many requests are simple, and a short answer is enough for them. Which two changes meet both constraints?
options: Move all requests to a larger model at high effort.
Set effort lower for simple requests, and keep medium effort for the rest.
Enable fast mode on Claude Haiku 5.5, which cuts the first-token wait.
Ask for a shorter answer in the prompt when output length adds time.
items.rationale: Lower effort cuts output and thinking work on simple requests. A shorter answer cuts output time, and medium effort keeps the accuracy floor on harder requests.
items.trap: A larger model looks like the safer choice for accuracy, but each call takes longer and can miss the latency target (Inference).
